approach: Write each particle's acceleration along its own wire as a vector using horizontal and vertical parts, then subtract the two vectors to get the relative acceleration.

steps.text: Each particle's acceleration along its wire equals g times the cosine of the wire's angle from the vertical.
steps.equation: a₁ = g cos30°, a₂ = g cos60°

steps.text: Write these as vectors, since the two wires point in different directions on the same side of the vertical.
steps.equation: a₁ = g cos30°(sin30°, cos30°), a₂ = g cos60°(sin60°, cos60°)

steps.text: The horizontal parts of the two vectors come out equal, so they cancel when the vectors are subtracted.
Subtract the vertical parts to get the size of the relative acceleration.
steps.equation: a_rel = g cos²60° − g cos²30° = g/4 − 3g/4 = −g/2, magnitude g/2

common_mistakes.text: Taking the first particle's own acceleration along its wire, g cos30° = √3g/2, as if it were the relative acceleration.
